why: A transpose takes no params; its speed depends on the block shape and the memory layout of the call. XNNPACK's transpose operator calls the ukernel on 32x32 tiles (transpose_config.x32.tile_size = 32 on RISC-V) with the full matrix strides; XNNPACK's own bench calls it once on a whole dense block. Both are in the matrix, plus sub-tensor views with odd leading dimensions.
reference_why: the scalar kernel XNNPACK falls back to on RISC-V without vectors; the check itself compares with the definition of a transpose

regimes.why: XNNPACK's bench: one ukernel call over the whole dense block
XNNPACK's transpose operator on a dense matrix: 32x32 tiles, full-matrix strides
the operator on a sub-tensor view: odd leading dimensions, rows not 64-byte aligned

check_extra.why: small tiles: many calls with block sizes at and below the kernel's own tile
a tile larger than every upstream kernel's tile and not a power of two
one call on a padded view: the padding between output rows must stay untouched

noise_why: A/A of identical kernels in one session (2026-10-28, aligned build): worst cell 0.83% (1024x1024, DRAM-bound), others <= 0.55%
